correctness.rationale: The two-chart degree-2 flat covering proves properness and genus; T_n'=nU_{n-1} has n-1 simple critical points with alternating signs. Repeated-root analysis exhausts 0,±2, each root double; central component graph, normalization genus, and local node structure follow. Discriminant exponents come from exact product/discriminant/resultant identities, not finite tests. The affine total space is isomorphic to the Cayley cubic, whose four ordinary quadratic nodes are the only total singularities, and infinity sections are smooth. The exact checker passes degrees 2 through 8 only; the general proof is written.

originality.rationale: Mascarin (arXiv:2611.15725v1) establishes the unshifted n=2 Cayley/parabolic-cylinder intersection but not the all-degree translated stable fibration, its complete bad-fiber list, discriminant factors, or total-space singularities. The genus-two three-node central degeneration has precedent (MathOverflow 262818); the claim is not that special case alone. Searches returned related Chebyshev curves and other nodal pencils but no implication covering the specified fixed-Cayley all-n claim. Priority remains qualified, as missing indexing is possible.
residual_risks: Classical or unindexed sources might already state the same all-degree fibration, perhaps under Fricke, Markov or trace-character variety terminology.
Search results show prior knowledge of the special n=2 limit; it is not claimed as independently new.
Some thematically similar published-finding corpus results were assessed from exact search summaries rather than full text because their defining families differ decisively.

value.rationale: Motivated by Mascarin's two-component Cayley/Chebyshev intersection, the theorem completely classifies the natural one-parameter translated cylinder fibration for all genera, including all stable boundary graphs, precise discriminant orders and a fixed-four-node total space. It distinguishes a single reducible special limit from two integral nodal degenerations and provides precise input for boundary-moduli and generalized-Jacobian calculations; this is not a mere numerical or parameter substitution.
